name: IEC astable element
summary: IEC element marked G, an astable that produces a continuous pulse train; drawing the waveform is optional.
description: The astable element is marked with G, optionally followed by a sketch of the output waveform. It produces a free-running pulse train. Variants include !G for a synchronously starting astable and G! for one that stops only after completing a pulse, as listed in TI's public overview.

Astable elements represent oscillators on logic diagrams: flasher circuits for indicator lamps, test pulse generators and clock sources. Where an enable input exists, its effect on the output at start and stop should be considered because the variant qualifiers describe exactly that.
The symbol does not state frequency or duty cycle. Note those values beside the element or reference the timing components.
readingNotes: Check for ! before or after G, which changes start or stop behaviour.
Find frequency and duty cycle in notes or timing parts.
drawingChecklist: Use !G or G! where start or stop behaviour matters.
distinction: A monostable produces one pulse per trigger; an astable runs continuously while enabled.
